screens_reviewed: Single capture of the Dashboard (tabs index) at top scroll position, dark theme, iPad portrait.
verdict: The dashboard renders cleanly in dark theme with a coherent warm palette, working metric grid, and consistent use of the ScaledText/ScaledParagraph primitives. However on iPad it is essentially a centered single-column phone layout: it never uses the tablet support-rail / two-pane tokens the design system defines for exactly this screen, and the shared TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE (1.3) is never applied, so type reads phone-sized on the large canvas.

critical_issues.issue: ScaledText/ScaledParagraph scale numeric fontSize/lineHeight only by the user fontScale preference (default 1). The design system defines TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE = 1.3 specifically so default tablet text is immediately legible, but nothing on this screen (or in the Scaled primitives) multiplies by it. On iPad every label, body, metric, and the Dashboard title therefore render at phone point sizes on a much larger viewport, making the screen feel like a scaled-up phone UI.
critical_issues.evidence: core.md:792 (TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE = 1.3 with comment 'applied on tablet screens'); core.md:2295-2321 (ScaledText/ScaledParagraph multiply only by fontScale, never by the tablet base scale); index.tsx:25,39 imports Scaled primitives and useDesignSystem but never reads isTablet for type sizing
critical_issues.fix: Either fold TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE into the scale used by ScaledText/ScaledParagraph when layout.isTablet (e.g. read useResponsiveLayout and multiply scaleSize by the tablet base), or expose the multiplier through useDesignSystem().fontScale so every screen picks it up. Confirm fontScale source actually compounds with the tablet base.

critical_issues.issue: The responsive token set defines homePageSupportRailWidth (250-290px) and twoPaneGap explicitly for this home screen, but index.tsx renders one centered column and never branches on layout.isTablet to build a support rail / two-pane (status + assigned-places) layout. On iPad the result is a tall single column with the four metric cards as the only horizontal use of space — a large-canvas adaptation opportunity (master-detail / rail) is missed.
critical_issues.evidence: core.md:818,836 (homePageSupportRailWidth 250/290 defined per tier); index.tsx:110-119 single ScrollView with getResponsiveContentContainerStyle and no isTablet layout branch; rendered screenshot shows a single full-width column
critical_issues.fix: On layout.isTablet, split the YStack into a two-column XStack using layout.twoPaneGap and layout.homePageSupportRailWidth — e.g. assigned-places list as the main pane and the online/offline + offline-readiness + metric cards as a fixed-width rail — or at minimum widen the metric grid to 4-up on tablet.

improvements.suggestion: narrow-tablet contentMaxWidth is 1040px while iPad portrait is ~768-834px wide, so getAdaptiveHorizontalPadding never produces centering gutters and content runs effectively edge-to-edge with only ~28px padding (matches the screenshot). Consider a tighter reading-width for single-column content on tablets so lines like the address/body copy don't stretch the full width.
improvements.evidence: responsive-layout.ts:662-673 (gutters only appear when windowWidth > resolvedMaxWidth); responsive-layout-tokens.ts:779 NARROW_TABLET_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH = 1040; screenshot shows full-bleed single column

improvements.location: app/(tabs)/index.tsx:300-309 metric XStack; MetricCard width="48%" minWidth 160
improvements.suggestion: Metric cards are hard-coded to width 48% (2x2). On the wider iPad canvas a single row of four cards would use horizontal space better and shorten the scroll. Drive the card width from layout.isTablet rather than a fixed 48%.
improvements.evidence: index.tsx:606 (width="48%", minWidth 160); screenshot shows 2x2 grid with empty vertical space

improvements.suggestion: Header avatar and the two icon buttons use fixed 44/42px sizes that do not scale on tablet. They meet the 44pt minimum but feel small on iPad; consider sizing from layout (e.g. layout.compactControlHeight, 44-46 on tablet) for visual balance with the larger canvas.
improvements.evidence: index.tsx:124-125,157-158,177-178 fixed pixel sizes; responsive-layout-tokens.ts:842 compactControlHeight tablet 46

tamagui_notes: index.tsx mixes Tamagui shorthand spacing tokens ($4, $6, $2.5, etc.) with raw pixel values from designSystem.radii/colors and inline style objects (boxShadow, backgroundColor) — consistent with the codebase pattern, but the screen-padding token (spacing.screenPaddingHorizontal 15 in design-system.ts:432) is bypassed in favor of getResponsiveContentContainerStyle, which is correct for tablet.

ActionButton hardcodes rgba(255,255,255,0.1)/0.16 backgrounds and borders (index.tsx:665,671) instead of theme tokens; on the green primary card this is intentional for contrast but is not theme-aware (core.md:342 darkColors has no matching token).
Screen correctly uses the ScaledText/ScaledParagraph primitives from design_system_components_used (index.tsx:25) rather than raw tamagui Text/Paragraph — good consistency.
borderColor="rgba(71, 203, 175, 0.18)" (index.tsx:314) is a one-off literal not present in darkColors; the adjacent bg uses designSystem.colors.primary, so the border is an un-tokenized magic value.
platform_notes: Safe area / status bar: top inset is handled at the root via Stack contentStyle paddingTop:20 (core.md:1378) plus contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior="automatic" on the ScrollView (index.tsx:113); the iPad status bar (5:27 PM / battery) sits clear of the avatar row in the screenshot — no clipping.

Tab bar uses bottom navigation on iPad (app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx) with tablet tweaks (icon size 22, label 12px, rounded items). This is an iOS-appropriate pattern for iPad; no Android nav-rail concern here.

iPad large-canvas adaptation is partial: padding/gaps interpolate up via tokens and the metric grid wraps, but there is no multi-column/master-detail and type is not up-scaled, so the net effect reads as a centered phone screen.
not_assessable: Exact contrast ratios — estimated only. The muted-foreground body text (e.g. 'Last sync ...' and date label) on the dark surface looks close to the AA threshold for small text but cannot be confirmed without measurement; no pair is clearly below AA so none is flagged as critical.
Loading/empty/error and offline states (Spinner, EmptyStateCard, offline warning card) are not exercised in this single online capture.
Exact iPad model/viewport width, and whether the user has raised fontScale, cannot be read from the image — typography findings assume default fontScale = 1.
Split-view / Slide Over and landscape orientation behavior are not shown.
score_rationale: Usable with clear problems: the screen is visually polished, theme-consistent, uses the shared Scaled primitives, and respects safe areas, but on iPad it fails to apply the design system's own tablet typography base scale and never uses the home-screen support-rail/two-pane tokens, leaving it a centered, under-scaled phone layout on the large canvas. Two real responsive-layout/typography gaps grounded in code keep it from the 7-8 band.
